rca.rootCause: SQLFluff's Jinja templater has custom logic that attempts to detect undeclared Jinja variables and report them as 'Undefined jinja template variable' errors. This custom undefined-variable check does not account for Jinja's block-assignment syntax (`{% set some_var %}...{% endset %}`, added in Jinja 2.8). It only recognizes the standard assignment form (`{% set some_var = value %}`). When a variable is defined via block assignment (especially inside an `{% if %}` block), the custom check fails to register it as defined, producing false 'Undefined jinja template variable' errors for subsequent references to that variable. The fix needs to make the undefined variable detection logic more sophisticated to recognize block-assignment set statements as variable definitions.
evidence: Issue title: 'sqlfluff doesn't recognise a jinja variable set inside of "if" statement'

# Remove variables that are defined within the template itself via
        # assignment (including block assignments). Jinja's static analysis
        # (meta.find_undeclared_variables) does not account for block
        # assignments (``{% set x %}...{% endset %}``), so we do it here.
        defined_in_template = self._find_variable_definitions(syntax_tree)
        undefined_variables -= defined_in_template

        if undefined_variables:
            # Lets go through and find out where they are:
            for val in self._crawl_tree(syntax_tree, undefined_variables, in_str):
                violations.append(val)
